gate: G-CLASSBIND (folded into G-AUDIT as calibration evidence)
authority: worker measurement only; no canonical write, no repair applied, no gate verdict, no node completion, no validation_status=passed
pre_registration_note: Written before the first census run. Field names and class/axis vocabulary were read during scoping; the classification rules, the control set and the predictions below were fixed before run_census() was first executed on the pinned inputs.
question: For the four frozen formulation classes, does the axis-level separation declared in the canonical F0 disjointness table agree with (a) the class axis values actually recorded in the same file, and (b) the supplement disjointness_matrix basis prose and axis_registry freezes? Every claim is bound to measured bytes.
pin_note: Every pin above is the sha256 measured on disk at registration time; the runner re-measures all eight and fails closed (exit 2) on any drift before it measures anything.

rule_set.R1_pair_set: The unordered pair set of canonical F0 `disjointness` must equal the unordered pair set of supplement `disjointness_matrix.pairwise`.
rule_set.R2_declared_decisive: For every canonical row and every axis named in `decisive_axes`, the two classes' canonical `classes[*].axes[axis]` values must differ. Verdicts: DIFFERS, EQUAL (declared-but-equal, a finding), MISSING_AXIS.
rule_set.R3_undeclared_separator: Any axis key present in either class's canonical `axes` map that is not in `decisive_axes` and whose two values differ is recorded as an UNDECLARED_SEPARATOR (info, not a defect).
rule_set.R4_basis_vs_decisive: The supplement basis prose is token-mapped to axes by the pre-registered phrase table; the resulting axis set is compared to the canonical decisive_axes set: SUBSET (agree), SUPERSET (finding), CROSS (finding), DISJOINT_NONEMPTY (finding), EMPTY (unmapped).
rule_set.R5_registry_vs_canonical: For each supplement axis_registry entry whose key maps to a canonical axes key (regularity_axis->regularity_token, genericity_axis->genericity_kind), the frozen value for a class is compared to that class's canonical value: MATCH, TOKEN_DIFFERS (finding), ABSENT.
rule_set.R6_status_field: Each class's canonical `genericity_value_status` is recorded verbatim next to the two genericity tokens; no verdict is derived from it, it is context for R5.

predictions.prediction: The canonical and supplement pair sets are EQUAL (6 unordered pairs each).
For all 6 canonical rows and every declared decisive axis, the canonical values DIFFER (no EQUAL and no MISSING_AXIS).
At least one UNDECLARED_SEPARATOR exists; expected on the AF-WCC-SCALAR-SPH pairs via genericity_kind (unresolved vs provisional_baire_residual).
R5 reports TOKEN_DIFFERS for the three vacuum classes on genericity_axis: supplement frozen 'residual_comeager' vs canonical axes.genericity_kind 'provisional_baire_residual'.
Every supplement basis axis set is a SUBSET of the canonical decisive_axes set for the same pair (no SUPERSET/CROSS/DISJOINT).
No canonical row declares an axis absent from both class axis maps (no MISSING_AXIS).

controls.expected: runner preflight exits 2 before any measurement

falsifier: Any byte move in a pinned input voids the binding. A reviewer exhibiting a canonical decisive-axis cell or supplement frozen value that the extractor misreads (false negative), or a verdict reported for a cell whose anchor text is not on disk (false positive), falsifies that cell. A pin drift between registration and measurement voids the whole census.
stop_rule: Stop when the 6-row axis census, the R1-R6 verdicts, the control table and the report are emitted with measured hashes, and the worker checkpoint is written. Out-of-scope needs (repairs, gate language) are filed as a blocker, not actioned.
non_claims: Not a gate verdict and not a node transition; A1/G-CLASSBIND/G-FORM/G-F0 remain owned by the controller and leads.
No claim about the truth of any formulation class or of cosmic censorship.
The disjointness table separates CLASS DESCRIPTORS, not data spaces (canonical disjointness_scope); this census does not test data-space overlap.
Structural declaration-level measurement only; it does not adjudicate whether a declared decisive axis is semantically decisive for physics.
